title: The amendment appraisal calls a content-weakening amendment progressive, and the verdict depends on whether claims are encoded
recommendation: Treat a new proposition on a pair the prior already relates as old content unless it fixes a sign the prior left open. Say in the help and the result text that the verdict is conditional on the encoded claims and the recorded outcomes. Second reader: Rest the finding on the sign-reversal case (c1b) and the replacement case (V2) rather than on the parallel weaker proposition. Recommendation: for each retained prediction that has a claim, compare the verdicts of the prior and new graphs. Count entailed to undetermined as content lost, and entailed to contradicted for a corroborated prediction as content lost and a new anomaly. Compare signed effects between the versions as discriminate() already does. Until then, say in the help and the result text that the verdict does not read the signs the propositions state.

title: The amendment appraisal does not read signs, so a reversal that contradicts a corroborated prediction is judged progressive

The scope item passes a boundary condition reading 'always'
Cyclic sign verdicts can be wrong in stable linear models; the stated assumption does not exclude it
component: entailments(), discriminate() and prediction_verdicts() under cycles='sigma'; walk_signs (entailment.py:83-124)
recommendation:
State the assumption precisely in API_SPEC.md §31, the entailments docstrings (both languages), methodology.Rmd:254 and the app help: the system with the intervened construct held fixed must be stable (spectral radius of B without the edges into x below 1); stability of the observational system is not enough. Alternatively assume rho(|B|) < 1, under which no violation occurred in 206,880 draws. Optionally return 'undetermined' for effects whose x lies in a component that is not one simple cycle, unless the walks there are all of one sign and stability after intervention is assumed explicitly. Second reader: The documentation is ambiguous rather than plainly insufficient:
- API_SPEC.md:1247 makes the positive factor depend on |g| < 1 for a simple component, and held_walks uses the components of the graph without the edges into x. There, y -> z -> y is a simple loop with gain 1.1, which violates that condition.
- The spec also assumes each loop 'settles' to a unique equilibrium. After do(x) the y-z loop does not settle: the do(x = 1) dynamics reach y = 1.4e5 and z = 1.5e5 after 200 steps, rising in the direction theoryforge gives. The value -11 is an unstable solution of the equations that is never reached.

The configuration is also rare. It needs x in a component that is not one simple cycle, a self-amplifying sub-loop stabilised only through x, and the non-default cycles='sigma'. It covered 0.13% of broadly sampled draws (1,045 of 797,200).

Keep the recommendation, which is a one-sentence change worth making before release: require the system with x held fixed to be stable. Grade it minor. The lens's citation API_SPEC.md:1061 for the definition of a loop points to the return-shape JSON; the definition is at line 1071.

title: 'identified' reports adjustment only and is false for many effects the ID algorithm identifies
component: entailments() identified/adjustment (entailment.py:351-395); preregistration 'Adjustment for an observational test' (prereg.py:365-371)
recommendation:
Rename the field, or document it as 'adjustment_identified'. Report the zero effect as identified, or mark it 'effect zero by the graph', when x is not an ancestor of y. For 0.9.0, add an ID-algorithm check (as y0 and causaleffect implement) so that 'identified' means identifiable. Second reader: Fix the denominator. ID identifies 88,062 of the 91,778 claims, so theoryforge says false in 27,058 of 88,062, not 'of 91,778 claims that ID identifies'.

For the 26,727 effects that are zero by the graph, ID's P(y | do(x)) = P(y) follows from the graph's own assertion that x does not cause y, which is the claim an observational test would examine. The preregistration's 'none suffices' is therefore the right advice for test planning. Drop the recommendation to report these as identified; marking them 'zero by the graph' is fine.

The substantive gap is the 331 claims (0.36%) that ID identifies and adjustment cannot. 'Front-door type' is a loose label for them, since they may include other identifications that do not use adjustment.

title: Adjustment sets are reported for effects whose exposure or outcome is unobserved

title: implications() ignores latent marks: untestable statements, and some testable ones missed
recommendation: Add an option, or a default for theories with latent marks, that projects out latent constructs (the latent projection in entailment._project is already verified) and derives the testable statements among observed constructs, as dagitty does. Mark statements that involve a latent construct as untestable without a measure. Second reader: API_SPEC.md:1473 does document that statements may hold a latent construct fixed and need a measure of it. Only the missed testable statements are undocumented.

title: Positive sign means non-negative outside strictly monotone models, and a crossover moderator silently breaks the one-direction assumption
component: Sign calculus assumptions (API_SPEC.md:1325; relation table API_SPEC.md:1109-1128)
recommendation: Say that the signs need strict monotonicity for 'positive', 'negative' and 'nonzero', and weak monotonicity for the non-strict reading. Say that a moderator which can reverse an effect (crossover or qualitative interaction) voids the sign of the moderated relation. Consider a warning when an outcome has a 'moderates' parent and a signed parent. Second reader: In the saturation example the verdict is not wrong: the computed effect, 3.3e-6, is positive and nonzero. It shows that 'nonzero' carries no magnitude. An exactly zero effect would need x bounded below 2. The inverted U is a mislabelled relation, not a failure of the derivation. Only the crossover case is a real violation, and it breaks the user's own 'increases' proposition.

title: Assumptions are absent where verdicts are consumed
component: Preregistration and dossier claim lines (entailment.py:565-591), README.md
recommendation: Add one sentence to the preregistration and dossier sections that print verdicts, naming the assumptions (linear or uniformly monotone relations, no omitted common causes, and for loops a unique equilibrium and stability after intervention). Add the same sentence to the README. Second reader: The lens says the app help states the unique equilibrium and the dying-out of loops. No text under apps/ mentions loop stability for signs. apps/shared/app-core.js mentions a unique equilibrium only for implications and feedback reading (lines 50, 624, 730 and 752), and the entailments help (lines 55 and 581) gives no assumption for cyclic graphs. The claim lines (entailment.py claim_line) also omit faithfulness, even where the verdict depends on it.

title: Sigma-based 'nonzero' conditional associations are zero in every linear cyclic model with the graph
recommendation: Note in §31 and §27 that, under sigma, 'nonzero' for a d-separated pair assumes a nonlinear model. Linear models with the graph imply independence there. Optionally report the d-separation status as well.

title: Testing the implied independencies by linear partial correlation is invalid under nonlinearity
component: Guidance on testing implications (app-core.js:580; planned 0.9.0 data tests)
recommendation: When data tests of implications are added (0.9.0), use or offer nonparametric conditional-independence tests (for example a generalised covariance measure or a kernel test) alongside latent-variable tests. State that linear partial correlations test the linear-Gaussian version of the statement.

title: derivation_chain accepts claims the causal reading never evaluated, including one the sigma reading contradicts
recommendation: Read cyclic theories with cycles='sigma' in the checklist, or count 'not_evaluated' claims as not verified.

title: A claimed zero against an undetermined derivation is reported as contradicted, a verdict that holds only under faithfulness
recommendation: Report 'undetermined', or 'contradicted only if no paths cancel', and do not fail the blocker on it.

title: discriminate() says each independence record can tell the two graphs apart, which needs faithfulness
The README does not say that every pair the theory leaves unjoined is read as an implied independence
A prediction that restates its one proposition, or a nonzero claim through unsigned edges, is entailed and passes derivation_chain
Amendment appraisal counts a recorded pass as corroboration even when the package's own post-data severity is 0
recommendation: Report, beside the verdict, each corroborating pass whose post-data severity is below 0.5 (or a stated threshold), and have validate(full=TRUE) warn when passed: true and the estimate lies outside the bounds; consider letting such a pass not count as corroboration. Second reader: The summary says the estimate lies 'six standard errors outside the claimed region'. It lies 4 (estimate 0.10 against a lower bound of 0.30, se 0.05). The recommended flag at severity below 0.5 catches only estimates at or beyond a bound. A pass inside the region that cannot be told apart from the bound (severity 0.6 to 0.8) would still count as full corroboration, so the threshold should be stated and justified, not fixed at 0.5.

title: The bow comment says a path is not identified when the theory already supplies an instrument
recommendation: Reword to 'may not be identified unless an instrument for x is present', or test identification (numerical Jacobian rank at random values, or the half-trek criterion of Foygel et al., 2012) and report the result. Second reader: Severity minor, not major. The recommendation stands: say 'may not be identified unless an instrument for x is present', or test identification and report the result. A rule that would get all 300 cases right is: no parent of x that is not also a parent of y, with the bow as the only bidirected edge on those vertices.

recommendation: Rename to claim-form riskiness (deprecating computed_severity and the 'Severity' headings), make interval and point scores depend on the width of the bounds relative to a declared plausible range or drop the numeric scale, and stop declared values from overriding the rubric in the checklist. Second reader: The module docstring (scoring.py:1-7) and the spec heading of section 9 already call this the 'claim-form riskiness rubric', and API_SPEC.md:409 concedes 'Despite its name'. The rename is therefore half done. What remains is the function name severity(), the field computed_severity and the 'Severity' headings of the preregistration and dossier.

title: Small-sample and parameter-dependent overstatement of post-data severity is not in the help or the app
recommendation: Add the caveat to the function help and the app reading now; later add an optional df (central or noncentral t, as in Spanos 2024, section 2.3) and say that se must describe the sampling distribution at the bound (or use a variance-stabilising scale). Second reader: The lens says the caveat is absent from the help and the app. Both do name the approximation. The help says 'The computation is a normal approximation to the sampling distribution of the estimate' (scoring.py:184, scoring.R:204). The app says 'under a normal approximation with the recorded standard error' (app-core.js:575) and 'It uses a normal approximation' (app-core.js:45). What they lack is the direction and size of the bias in small samples, and the requirement that se describe the sampling distribution at the bound.

title: Simulation verdicts for cyclic theories are set by default knobs the theory does not state, and the help and app do not say so

Second reader: The app does name 'gain k outweighs the damping' (app-core.js:1062-1063), but only in the message shown when a run stops on a non-finite state. With the app's maximum of 500 steps and its default settings, that message is rarely reached, so the substance of the finding stands.

Second reader: The lens missed a third location. The app's operation help (apps/shared/app-core.js:45) also attributes the nearer-bound computation, which is the two-bound rule, to '(Mayo & Spanos, 2006)'.

title: The time window, as well as gain against damping, decides the qualitative picture, and neither the help nor the app says so
Bounds carry no scale, so an estimate on a different scale from the bounds goes undetected
A recorded pass is never reconciled with its estimate, standard error, alpha and sidedness
validate(full=True) accepts a point or interval prediction without bounds, which the rubric then scores highest
Empty, circular and refuted theories outscore strong ones, under every weighting tried
recommendation: Stop presenting the aggregate as a rigour rating. Rename it as specification coverage, or remove it from the headline. Show the item profile with each item's basis (label, presence or checked). Before any number is called rigour, run a validation study: several coders encoding the same sources, known groups of corroborated and refuted or pseudoscientific theories, and agreement with expert appraisal. Second reader: Call the evidence an adversarial demonstration by one encoder, not a failed known-groups validation. Rest the finding on rt1 and rt2 and move rt3 to the test-record finding. Report the share of weight on labels or field presence as 0.52 to 0.76, depending on how the items are classed. Correct the claim that the conscientious re-encodings add nothing the sources lack.

Note that rigor.py:78 reads outcomes for a type check.

title: Declaring and omitting raise the score, and specifying lowers it

Remove parsimony from the scored total and leave it to appraise_amendment. Use only the rubric in risk_severity and show the declared value beside it. Check interval and point bounds against a declared scale range. Second reader: Drop the invented outcome as evidence. Describe the prospect-theory block as a correct verdict on the encoded graph that leaving out the claim avoids. Add the double counting of a named rival. Say that checking bounds against a scale needs a schema extension.

recommendation: Print no decimals, or report coarse bands. Do not invite comparison of theories closer than about 5 points. Say in the app that close scores are not distinguishable. Second reader: Severity minor. Add the app's two-decimal sentence and its inconsistency with the chip. Describe the one-judgement figures as illustrative, not as an estimate of inter-coder reliability.

title: aggregate_range understates how far the score depends on its conventions

If a number is kept, replace the range with a stated Monte Carlo interval over weights, such as Dirichlet centred on the defaults, plus a note that coding judgement adds more. Second reader: Verdict 'sound with caveats', severity minor. Keep the range. Say in the report and dossier that it is the extremes of one-at-a-time weightings and not an interval, and that coding judgements and rubric constants lie outside it.

recommendation: Extend the types (for example equation, probabilistic, decision-theoretic, computational), require a spec_ref that resolves, or rename the item as 'formal model declared'. Second reader: Severity minor. Move the point that a label earns the item without a model to the first finding.

recommendation: Document that discrimination is judged by sign and separation only. Let a rival's bounds count where both state a region.

title: Thresholds flip item statuses without moving the score
recommendation: Show the item scores rather than counts of statuses, or mark the statuses near a threshold.

recommendation: Keep, and print the maturity next to the gate wherever the gate is shown.

title: The methodology page lists the outcomes of tests among what a score difference reflects, although check() does not read them
The app's interpretation sentence pads the score to two decimals while the chip shows one
The dossier labels the number 'Aggregate rigour score'
One prediction's type label feeds three items carrying 38 per cent of the aggregate, so the twelve items are not independent
The lexical redundancy screen passes mutually circular definitions
The schema cannot state a rival's quantitative prediction
The amendment appraisal labels an accommodation of the anomaly's own data 'progressive'
recommendation: Before release, qualify every statement that the verdict is 'in Lakatos's sense' (index.md:56-57, README.md:114-116, methodology.md:7, app-core.js:577 and 701). Say that the appraisal cannot tell prediction from accommodation and reads neither dates nor data provenance. Later, add an optional per-outcome record of whether the data were collected after the prediction and used in building the amendment, require it for 'progressive' (or report 'progressive (accommodation not excluded)'), and require SEV at or above a threshold for a pass to count. Second reader: Rest the 'wrong' verdict on C1, not on D1 and D2, and add C3 as a second instance. Name develop.py:364 ('pid not in protected') as the mechanism through which a self-declared 'protects' entry creates new content. Add to the release fix that the paraphrase of Lakatos should restore 'novel'.

title: Appraised step by step, a prediction made in one version and corroborated in the next is never credited, while recording both at once is
recommendation: Before release, document that a prediction must be appraised against the version before it was stated, and warn when the new version's predictions carry outcomes whose prediction was untested in the prior. For 0.9, add a function that appraises a chain of versions, carries each prediction's version of origin and credits its later corroboration to the amendment that introduced it. Second reader: Reframe the finding. Applied step by step, the appraisal first calls a bold, independently testable auxiliary 'degenerating', then never revises that verdict. Recording the corroboration in the same version as the amendment gives 'progressive'. Besides the history function, an untested independent prediction should give a pending class rather than ad_hoc2. The app's prior caution should say that the prior must be the version before the prediction was stated.

title: A declared 'severity' of any value passes the risk_severity item
recommendation: Score the item from the rubric (or from a bounds-based riskiness) alone, and report the declared value beside it without counting it. At the least, document that a declared value overrides the rubric and can raise the item to a pass. Second reader: Withdraw 'at the least, document' and the release-critical flag, because the documentation and the dossier already do this. The remaining recommendation, that check() should report the declared value beside the item without scoring it, is a 0.9 matter.

title: The checklist's ad hoc test is cleared by citing an old success, unlike the appraisal
recommendation: Rename the item (for example 'ad_hoc_rescue'). Without a prior version, count as support only predictions that the assumption is needed to derive and that are not the anomaly, or make the item advisory and point to appraise_amendment. Document the loophole now. Second reader: Not release-critical. Keep the rename and the advisory wording.

title: Diagnosticity credits a prediction whose success would favour the rival
recommendation: Count a prediction only when the theory's verdict is 'entailed' and the rival's is not, report declared-only rivals separately, drop the rubric bonus when the declaration is shown false, and correct the app sentence. Second reader: Downgrade to minor and drop the release flag, except for the app sentence. Choose one criterion for the checklist and discriminate(): either 'entailed against contradicted' throughout, or a documented weaker 'entailed against not entailed'.

title: Weakening is judged by the type label, so relabelling escapes the degenerating rule
recommendation: When both versions state bounds, compare the regions and ignore the label. Use the type rank only when neither version states bounds. Second reader: Severity minor. Keep the fix, but it need not block the release.

title: Corroboration ignores the recorded data, the severity of the test and the number of tests
recommendation: Report SEV beside each corroboration in the appraisal and warn when a pass has SEV below 0.5. For 0.9, define corroboration with a severity threshold and report counts of passes and failures instead of 'mixed'. Second reader: Restate the finding as 'the appraisal never reads severity'. Record that the D2 inconsistency is flagged in the dossier but not in appraise_amendment() or the app. Add that even a severity threshold would not catch C1, because the nominal SEV ignores selection effects.

title: Riskiness and precision read labels, not regions, and misorder claims about one quantity
recommendation: Add an optional Spielraum to a prediction and compute riskiness as 1 - width/Spielraum (and precision from the same width), with the label rubric as a documented fallback. Before release, state in methodology.md that the Popperian order holds only for nested claims and that the rubric does not check nesting. Second reader: Narrow the documentation recommendation to the precision item and the app wording. The Spielraum-based measure remains the substantive fix.

title: The falsifiability blocker passes on a label
recommendation: Count a prediction as forbidding only when it states a region (bounds) or a signed claim, or have validate(full=True) require one of them for a directional prediction. Until then, describe the item as 'a prediction is labelled as forbidding'. Second reader: Add C7. Before release, validate(full=True) should refuse a directional type with a 'nonzero' claim, or the documentation should say that the item reads the label alone.

title: No hard core or programme history, so a reversal of the central claim is a 'progressive problemshift'
recommendation: State in the documentation that the appraisal does not tell belt from core and does not assess ad hoc3. Consider an optional 'core' flag on propositions and report an amendment that changes a core proposition as a change of programme, not a problemshift. Second reader: Note that D8 is partly an instance of finding 1, and cross-reference C4.

title: The appraisal verdict depends on how the anomaly was encoded
recommendation: Document the dependence, and have the appraisal note when a lost implication matches a failed prediction that states no claim, so that the user can add the claim. Second reader: Downgrade D7 to minor. Move the encoding concern to C2, which belongs with finding 1.

title: Mayo (1991) is cited to justify ignoring novelty, but severity is not read either
recommendation: Either read severity in the corroboration rule or rewrite the justification to say that the appraisal assesses neither novelty nor severity and that 'progressive' should be read with the test record. Second reader: Severity minor, as a communication fix within finding 1.

title: Meehl (1990a) is cited without its operational content
recommendation: For 0.9, report the prior's track record (corroborated risky predictions, with Ci where bounds and a Spielraum exist) beside each appraisal, and say in the documentation which parts of Meehl's paper the package uses.

title: The labels ad_hoc1 and ad_hoc2 come from Lakatos without attribution, and ad hoc3 is silently omitted
recommendation: Attribute the labels, define them as the package reads them (from 'protects' and the declared booleans) and state that ad hoc3 is not assessed.

title: post_data_severity does not check statistical adequacy, and its explication is contested
recommendation: Add one sentence on each to methodology.md and the docstring.

title: The Lakatos page reference and quotation were not verifiable in this audit
recommendation: Check the wording and page against Lakatos (1970) before release. Second reader: Reduce the remaining task to checking the 1970 page number.

title: Novelty can be manufactured without an anomaly, since a trivial assumption that lists an old prediction in 'protects' makes a replication progressive
The content-loss rule ignores implied signs, so reversing an unstated sign entailment loses no content
Whether a new prediction is new content or an articulation depends on whether it states a machine-readable claim
An auxiliary assumption with an untested independent prediction is classed ad_hoc2 and the amendment called degenerating
post_data_severity is nominal and ignores selection effects, and no document mentions them
validate(full=True) accepts a directional prediction whose claim has sign 'nonzero', and it passes the falsifiability blocker
The diagnosticity item and discriminate() use different criteria
The app's appraisal sentence does not report new anomalies when a progressive amendment loses a corroborated prediction
The headline number is presented as the rigour of a theory but measures declared field completion; hollow theories score 100 and pass the gate
recommendation: For 0.8.0, take '/100' and the score out of headlines: the app chip, the interpretation sentence, the dossier header, the rigour-grid title and the roadmap hub. Rename the aggregate, for example 'declared-specification index', and put the scope-and-limits paragraph in the check()/tf_check() help and the app's help and result note. Lead the report with the item profile. Mark each item's credit as 'checked' (graph verdict, numeric bounds, lexical screen), 'declared' (type label, severity, mechanism string, formal_model.type, a rival without propositions, maturity) or 'not assessed', with counts. Second reader: Add app-core.js:571 and 1807 to the list of places to change. The README sentence is at README.md:104, not 105.

title: Re-encodings that leave the theory itself unchanged move the score by up to 10.8 points; one theory spans about 19 points and the stated range ignores this
recommendation: Before release, reword methodology.md:9 and its Rmd twin to say 'the same theory file'. State in the help and the app that encoding choices move the aggregate by up to about 20 points and that differences below about 10 points are not interpretable. Print the aggregate as an integer. Later, either canonicalise encodings (count theory-level boundary conditions towards construct clarity, treat an interval at the limits of a declared scale as directional, merge entailed duplicates), or let the package report an encoding-sensitivity band from the transformations used here. Second reader: Say that single content-preserving re-encodings move the aggregate by 0.6 to 10.8 points, and combined ones by about 7 to 14 points for the two fixtures, or about 19 if per-construct boundary conditions are dropped. Replace 'differences below about 10 points are not interpretable' with: no study has established what difference is interpretable, and constructed re-encodings of one theory differ by several points. Rewording methodology.md:9 is still right, but see the reliability verdict check.

title: A feedback loop disables the derivation check and unblocks the gate
recommendation: Read the checklist's graphs with cycles='sigma' when the graph is cyclic, or report the affected predictions as 'not checked' and keep them out of the pass. At minimum, document the fallback in methodology.md beside the derivation chain and flag it in the report before release. Second reader: Severity critical, fix before release. The scope is any feedback loop anywhere in the propositions, not only a loop through the claim's variables. On the recommendation: sigma verdicts hold only when every loop settles to a unique equilibrium (methodology.md:258), so making sigma the checklist default imports that assumption. The minimum fix is to report such predictions as 'not checked (feedback loop)', keep them out of a pass, and offer sigma as an explicit, documented option.

title: Verification asymmetry: giving the package more to check can only cost points, and disclosure is strategic
recommendation: Report verified and unverified credit separately (for example 'derivation: 1 of 4 checked against the graph, 3 by references only'), and count only checked predictions towards a pass, or show unchecked ones as 'declared'. For parsimony, list the core assumptions that protect failed predictions as 'unclassified' instead of ignoring them, and show the assumptions whose added_for is null. Treat a 'protects' entry unrelated to the anomaly as declared, not as corroboration. Second reader: Replace 'can only cost points' with: never gains from a claim or a rival's propositions, and gains from added_for only when the assumption passes. Add the counts of 14 of 35 and 3 of 18. Name the eligibility mismatch with the amendment appraisal as the mechanism behind the 'protects' padding.

title: Self-declared type labels and severities control about 36 points; the package's own help example mislabels a claim
component: falsifiability, precision, risk_severity, claim-form rubric, validate
recommendation: Before release, correct the help example (type 'directional') in R and Python, and have validate(full) warn about a point or interval without two finite bounds. Make the rubric agree with the precision item, giving a point or interval without bounds no more than a directional claim. Later, measure precision against a declared scale range, as Meehl's intolerance (1 - I/S) does (described by Witte et al., 2022), and report declared severities beside the rubric without scoring them. Second reader: Say that labels plus bounds control up to about 36 points at the extremes, while single plausible relabellings move 1 to 4 points. Correct the example in tf_check and tf_report and regenerate the Rd files; there is no Python example to fix. Give the other R examples explicit bounds.

title: The checklist ignores phenomena, evidence and the test record; a theory whose every prediction failed keeps its score and gate
recommendation: Show, beside the profile and without folding them into it, the phenomena with each claim's verdict, the test record (passed, failed, registered) and post-data severity. Say at the point of use that the score does not read them. Second reader: Limit the fix-before-release part to a sentence at the point of use saying that the score and gate do not read phenomena, evidence or test outcomes. Showing the test record beside the profile is a 0.9.0 feature.

title: aggregate_range covers only one-at-a-time weight changes and reads as the uncertainty of the score
recommendation: Rename the range 'range under one-at-a-time reweighting', or vary all weights jointly. Never present it as the uncertainty of the score. For comparisons, report item-wise dominance: panic v2 dominates v1 and no weighting reverses them, whereas profiles that cross leave the order to the weights. Second reader: Severity minor. Describe the range as equal weights plus each weight halved or doubled in turn. Relabel the second scheme as checklist weights times independent Exp(1) factors.

title: The development roadmap turns the index into a target
recommendation: Rephrase the roadmap steps as substantive actions on named elements (for example 'state the region pred3 allows'). Mark items that a declaration alone can satisfy, and leave the points gained out of the roadmap. Second reader: Minor. Keep the recommendations: phrase steps as actions on named elements, mark the items a declaration alone can meet and drop the score from the hub.

title: No validity evidence of any of the five kinds
Wording of definitions moves the lexical redundancy item by 10.8 points
recommendation: Report redundancy flags as pairs to review, not as a scored item worth 0.10, or score them only after the user has confirmed them.

title: Item names that their own documentation says mislead
recommendation: Rename the items, for example to 'ad_hoc_auxiliaries' and 'claim_form_riskiness', keeping the old ids as aliases for one release.

title: Pass cut-offs follow no common logic, and aggregates with different coverage are compared
recommendation: Document the reason for each cut-off or harmonise them. Do not compare aggregates with different coverage, and show coverage next to any aggregate.

title: A feedback loop anywhere in the propositions, even one unrelated to the claim, sets every claim to not_evaluated and unblocks the gate
The parsimony item and the amendment appraisal treat a protected prediction differently
The app's reading guide and welcome text carry no caveat
The mislabelled order claim recurs in tf_report and the help pages, and three other R examples type a point claim with no bounds
The aggregate score ignores test outcomes and phenomena but is presented as rigour
recommendation:
For 0.8.0, add one sentence wherever the score is shown (report, dossier, app) saying that it reads neither test outcomes nor phenomena, and show the numbers of failed predictions and of contradicted phenomena next to it. For 0.9.0, consider the name 'specification checklist', and keep any future track-record index separate and unweighted until it has been validated. Second reader: Two corrections:
- Insensitivity to test outcomes is by design for a checklist applied before data, and methodology.Rmd:408 says so. The defect is the wording in the app, README and DESCRIPTION, together with the asymmetry between phenomena and predictions.
- Add a recommendation: let derivation_chain, or a new item, treat a contradicted phenomenon as it treats a contradicted prediction. Also cite app-core.js:39 and :1807.

title: The literature framing omits Eronen and Bringmann's diagnosis and their caveat about fat-handed interventions
No evidence on the reliability of encoding or on the validity of the appraisal
recommendation:
Plan three preregistered studies before 1.0:
(a) Inter-coder reliability: three or more trained coders encode the same 10 published verbal theories, and agreement is measured on constructs, propositions, implications, checklist items and verdicts.
(b) Concurrent validity of appraise_amendment(): its verdicts on documented episodes are compared with blind expert judgements.
(c) Predictive validity, as Faust and Meehl (1992) and Meehl (2002) propose: score versions of theories at one date and test whether the scores predict later corroboration or abandonment. Second reader: Plan the validation studies against a human baseline, not against perfect agreement:
- Bornmann et al. (2010; PLoS ONE 5(12), e14331; verified through Crossref and PubMed 21179459) report a mean ICC of .34 and a mean kappa of .17 for journal peer reviews.
- Grove et al. (2000; Psychological Assessment 12(1), 19-30; PubMed 10752360) find mechanical prediction 'about 10% more accurate' than clinical prediction on average.

Study (a) should therefore compare agreement between theoryforge encodings with the agreement between human appraisals of the same theories.

title: The related-tools page omits the closest precedents
Planned data tests: tests on observed scores would reject true theories
component: Planned expansion: testing implied independencies against data
recommendation:
Build the feature on latent-variable models: local tests on the compile_sem measurement model (Thoemmes et al., 2018), with observed-score tests only alongside a reliability warning. Offer equivalence tests of implied zeros with a stated smallest effect of interest (Lakens, 2017) besides nil tests. Report each statement with control for multiplicity and keep Shipley's C to the basis set. Use regression-based tests (generalised covariance measure) when the relations may be nonlinear. Record the results as test outcomes with estimate and se, and never feed them into the checklist score. Second reader: Three corrections:
- Report the common-set-up comparison above in place of the mixed figures.
- Correct the paraphrase of Shah and Peters (2020). Their abstract states that 'a valid test for conditional independence does not have power against any alternative' when Z is continuous, which is stronger than 'no uniformly valid test has power against every alternative'.
- Note that the latent route presupposes a correct measurement model. Kellen et al. (2021; abstract verified through Crossref): 'empirical means alone cannot determine this relationship' between concepts and observations.

title: Half the bundled implications rest only on the theory saying nothing about associations
recommendation: Mark each implication that rests only on an unstated association between exogenous constructs, for example with a 'rests_on' field. Ask authors to declare such associations, or to state the independence as an explicit claim, before any data test. Second reader: Cite app-core.js:580. Grade minor for 0.8.0, and make the marking a prerequisite of the planned data tests.

title: Planned ensemble simulation: results depend on the sampling distribution and ignore functional form
recommendation: Report the sign patterns the theory allows and forbids (parameter space partitioning; qualitative network analysis), with any share shown under at least two sampling distributions and labelled as conditional on them. Report the stable share and the regime boundaries. Include alternative functional forms before claiming robustness in the sense of van Dongen et al. (2025). Never present a share as the probability that the theory predicts a sign. Second reader: Recommend reporting the regime boundary in preference to stable shares, include moderation in any ensemble check, and test both directions of the sign rules.

title: The documented pgmpy testing route fails for theories with associations
recommendation: Say that pgmpy's metrics refuse the latent nodes and point to dagitty::localTests, which reads the bidirected edges of the causal_dag view directly (out/interop_theorytools.out, section 3).

title: read_dagitty silently drops augmented-DAG labels and functional forms
recommendation: Read label into label and form into functional_form, warn when an attribute is dropped, write both on export, and document the augmented-DAG convention of theorytools. Second reader: Say 'documented at methodology.Rmd:388 but not warned at run time' instead of 'silently'.

title: Constructs cannot point to external construct identifiers
recommendation: Add an optional list of external identifiers (DCT UCID, Cognitive Atlas, the behaviour-change intervention ontology), and offer import and export of DCT YAML and a FAIR-theory export (.zenodo.json with upload_type 'model' and keyword 'fairtheory', README, LICENSE, definitions.csv and the theory file).

title: The package description says the package tests theories
recommendation: Reword, for example as 'preparing tests of scientific theories and recording their outcomes'. Second reader: Add .github/landing.html:72 to the places to reword.

title: The VAST reference year disagrees with the registered metadata
recommendation: Check the journal's page and cite the year it gives, noting online-first and issue years if they differ. Second reader: Withdraw the finding, or at most note that Crossref's date for this record is anomalous.

title: A phenomenon the theory's own graph contradicts leaves the score and gate unchanged, while the same claim as a prediction blocks the gate
recommendation: Let derivation_chain, or a new item, treat a contradicted phenomenon as it treats a contradicted prediction.

title: Signs and claims reach data only through an assumed link from constructs to observations, and estimates are read as if on the construct's scale
Phenomena cannot record their evidential status, such as replication or robustness
Further passages present the checklist as judging quality
The score and gate are displayed as a quality judgement, with their limits shown nowhere near them
component: apps/shared/app-core.js:571, 653, 1639-1643; editor.js:859; rigour SVG (diagram.py:502, diagram.R:567); dossier header (API_SPEC §20)
recommendation:
For 0.8.0, in the app only:
- RESULT_GUIDE.check becomes: 'The checklist asks whether the file states what twelve criteria from the methodology literature call for, such as bounded predictions, defined constructs and a mechanism for each proposition. It checks that a field is filled in or a label is used and does not judge what the text says, so a false theory can score highly when its file is complete. The weights are a convention, so the range under other weightings is given. The gate reports only whether either blocking item failed. Read the item statuses first.'
- The card chip reads 'checklist 78.5 · gate pass', with the title 'How completely the file is specified against checklist 3.0. Not a judgement of the theory's truth or quality.'
- The start panel gains: 'These are checks of what the file states. None of them shows that a theory is true or well reasoned, and the checklist's weights and thresholds have not been validated against expert judgement.'
Later: carry the range onto the card (this needs the runtime glue to pass aggregate_range); put the theory id, checklist version, range and a footnote inside the rigour SVG; consider showing 'n of m applicable items pass' instead of the aggregate. Second reader: The claim that the limits are shown 'nowhere near' is too broad. At desktop width, the sidebar help is on screen beside the result. It carries the limit for entailments, discriminate, post-data severity and landscape (shots/py-cognitive-dissonance-04-discriminate.png, shots/py-happy-vowel-manchester-02-entailments.png). The gap lies in these: the checklist, the card, the editor, the dossier, the preregistration, the exported SVGs, the function help, report(format='html') and render_report().

The SVG subtitle is in default ink. Only the item swatches are green.

The proposed guide sentence 'It checks that a field is filled in or a label is used' is inaccurate:
- derivation_chain checks entailment by the causal graph;
- diagnosticity reads the rival's propositions;
- precision checks numeric bounds;
- non_redundancy measures lexical overlap.
Say instead that the checks read the presence, labels and structure of what the file states, and do not judge whether its content is true or sound.

Add that the score does not read test outcomes.

title: The dossier reads as an independent audit of author-entered claims
recommendation:
For 0.8.0, in the app:
- Rename the operation 'Dossier', with the description 'The file and its checks, for reviewers'.
- RESULT_GUIDE.dossier becomes: 'The dossier gathers what the theory file records and what the package derives from it. The score, gate and verdicts describe the file against fixed rules. The test outcomes, evidence, registrations and declared severities are as the author entered them, and the package does not verify them. It is not an independent audit.'
- The R and Python help of dossier() gains the same sentence.
In the package, in 0.8.0 if the goldens can be regenerated and otherwise 0.8.1, a fixed italic preamble after the header: '_Generated by theoryforge from the file with the content hash above. The checklist score and gate describe how completely the file is specified against checklist <v>, by rules that read fields and labels and do not judge their content, with weights that are conventions. Test outcomes, evidence, registrations and declared severities are as the author recorded them and are not verified. Equivalent models concern observational data only. This is not an independent audit and does not show that the theory is true._'
Also rename 'Aggregate rigour score' to 'Checklist score' and the heading to 'Equivalent models (observational data)'. Second reader: The preamble should also say which inconsistencies the dossier does cross-check: passes outside the region, and declared severity above the rubric. It should say that nothing else is cross-checked.

title: The docs say a passing gate shows the file states what a test would need, but a nearly empty file passes
recommendation: For 0.8.0, replace the sentence with: 'The score is a mean of the item scores under conventional weights, and the gate reports whether either blocking item failed. A passing gate shows only that at least one prediction is typed as a claim that rules some result out and that every prediction cites declared propositions. Neither shows that the theory is true or well reasoned.' Second reader: The lens's replacement sentence leaves out that derivation_chain also requires the graph to entail any claim a prediction states (rigor_checklist.yaml:74). Suggested wording: 'at least one prediction is labelled point, interval or directional, and every prediction cites declared propositions whose graph entails any claim it states; the labels are the author's and are not checked against the statements'. The worked example in index.md should say that the block reads the label.

title: The rival comparison colours 'entailed' green and 'contradicted' red, reading as a win for the theory
recommendation: For 0.8.0, use neutral pills (grey or blue) for the theory and rival columns, and for compelled and reversible. Append to RESULT_GUIDE.discriminate: 'The comparison shows which results would favour one account over the other. It does not say which account the data favour.' Second reader: Downgrade to minor. Neutral pills are still a cheap improvement.

title: A missing shared word is labelled 'under-theorised' and coloured red
component: apps/shared/app-core.js:587, 1086-1095; app.css:319; package landscape status values

title: The simulation's growth or decay is set by two free settings the display does not mention
recommendation:
For 0.8.0, in the app:
- Append to RESULT_GUIDE.simulate: 'The gain k and the damping are not stated by the theory, and together they decide whether a feedback loop grows or settles. The values have no unit, and the trajectory is not fitted to data.'
- In the reading, add 'At k = <k> and damping = <d> the values <grow|settle>; other settings can reverse this.', taking grow or settle from the last row against the first.
- In trajectoryChart, add the axis titles 'value (no unit)' and 'time step (dt = <dt>)' and a caption line, 'Linear system, k = <k>, damping = <d>, <method>. Not fitted to data.'
Later: have simulate() report the spectral abscissa and the damping at which the regime changes; run an ensemble over k and the damping. Second reader: 'Not fitted to data' is in methodology.md:385, not the README. The same paragraph says 'The regime of a theory with feedback loops is set by the gain against the damping'. It also says a linear system 'cannot show the bistability that formal models of panic disorder rely on'. The package documents the limit and the app omits it. The app should carry that sentence about bistability, since its showcase example is panic. The reading already discloses the offset of coincident lines (app-core.js:813), which the lens did not credit.

title: 'Entailed' is mostly a restatement but is shown as a green verdict
recommendation: For 0.8.0, append to RESULT_GUIDE.entailments: 'Entailed means the claim follows from the propositions as written, a check of the theory's internal consistency. It is not evidence that the claim is true, and a claim that restates one proposition is entailed trivially.' Make the pill neutral, and write 'none needed' in place of 'nothing', as the preregistration does. Later: a package field marking restatements. Second reader: Downgrade to minor as a communication issue. That most shipped predictions restate one proposition is a substantive point about derivational content, for the causal or philosophy lens. The lens's proposed guide text 'entailed trivially' should read 'entailed by that proposition alone, with no other path of opposite sign'.

title: Two different 'severity' quantities share one name, and the app label departs from the docs
component: apps/shared/app-core.js:42-43, 574; diagram.py:528-537; diagram.R:597-608; dossier severity section
recommendation:
For 0.8.0, in the app:
- Label the operation 'Claim-form rubric', with the description 'Pre-data riskiness of each claim's form'.
- Rename the 'computed severity' column 'rubric value'.
- In the guide, say the bonus goes to 'predictions that name a registered rival they are declared to discriminate from (the declaration is not checked)'.
Later: rename the label in the package's documents and SVG and write the values with one decimal. Second reader: Downgrade to minor. A related point the lens missed: risk_severity reads the author's declared severity in preference to the rubric, so an author-entered number moves the score.

title: The preregistration does not say it is partial and generated, and 'Derivations check: yes' overclaims
recommendation: Later, since it changes a byte-identical golden: an italic line after the header, '_Generated by theoryforge from the theory file. It holds the theory and hypotheses sections only; the design, sampling plan, analysis plan and inference criteria must be added before registration. A hypothesis marked already tested cannot be tested confirmatorily here. The content hash identifies the file and is not a time stamp._' Rename the header line 'Derivation references resolve and the graph entails every stated claim: yes'. Make the nested '## Preregistration: <title>' sit one level below its section heading. Second reader: The PRP-QUANT advice is not only in the app. It is in tf_preregister.Rd:73-75, prereg.py:452-454 and API_SPEC §11. The missing design and analysis sections are visible to anyone completing a registration, so the risk is an incomplete registration rather than a wrong scientific conclusion. Downgrade to minor.

title: Checklist criterion strings describe the concept, not what is checked
recommendation: Later, since it changes the goldens: 'At least one prediction is typed point, interval or directional' and 'Every proposition's mechanism field is filled in (its text is not judged)'. Review the other ten strings in the same way. Second reader: Only two of the twelve strings are at fault. construct_clarity, scope, formalisation, non_redundancy ('lexical screen') and diagnosticity ('declared') already say what is checked, so 'review the other ten in the same way' overstates the problem. The lens also missed that the HTML report's 'grounding' column attaches Popper, Meehl and Cronbach and Meehl to these checks.

title: Inconsistent and spurious number formats, and a tie reported as a single 'riskiest claim'

recommendation: Add a schema field for manipulated constructs, used as background knowledge for Meek's rules.

title: Every habit preregistration reports 'Derivations check: yes' while its claims are not evaluated or left open
recommendation: Give derivation_chain a distinct status when claims could not be read because of a loop: n/a for those predictions, or a warn with the count. Have preregister() and dossier() compute the header with the same cycles as their body. Update API_SPEC.md:522 to match.

title: The aggregate score agrees across encoders only because it measures form completion, and it does not separate the three theories
recommendation: State in README, methodology and the report that the aggregate indexes how completely a file is filled, and that it moves with encoding conventions. Advise against comparing aggregates across theories or authors without a shared encoding protocol. Report items before the aggregate. Consider leaving the aggregate out of the dossier header.

title: Implied independencies and equivalence classes describe one encoding, and alternative defensible encodings of the same text disagree
component: implications(), equivalent_models(), preregistration section on implied independencies
recommendation: Word these outputs as consequences of the encoded graph under the closed-world reading. Let a user mark an absent edge as 'not ruled out' rather than 'no effect'. Add a function that compares two encodings of one theory, reporting shared and conflicting edges, independencies and verdicts, so that sensitivity to encoding choices can be shown.

title: Encoding an interaction as 'moderates' erases the sign of a main effect the theory states
component: Relation semantics (moderates) and the encoding guidance
recommendation: Document the trade-off in the encoding guide now. Later, allow a moderation proposition to carry a signed main effect, or add an explicit interaction construct, so that both statements of a theory such as Triandis's can be encoded and checked.

title: The conservative sign reading in loops with more than one cycle turns into disagreement between encoders
recommendation: For small components, derive the sign of each total effect from the minors of (I - B) with sign sets. Otherwise mark such verdicts with a distinct basis (for example 'conservative_loop'), so that a reader can tell this case from a genuinely unsigned route.

title: The schema does not say when a stated relation is also a prediction, so the preregistered hypotheses vary threefold for one text
recommendation: Publish an encoding protocol with explicit rules: what becomes a construct, a proposition, a prediction, a phenomenon, an assumption or scope. In preregister(), list propositions that no prediction cites, as candidate hypotheses, so that the choice is visible.

title: Documentation says 'the same theory always gives the same result'
recommendation: Replace 'theory' with 'theory file' in these sentences. Add one sentence saying that different defensible encodings of one verbal theory give different results.

title: Hedges and the status of cited proposals are lost unless written into a statement
recommendation: Add a status field for predictions and propositions (for example 'untested', 'cited proposal', 'established') and print it in the preregistration and the dossier.

title: Severity rubric is constant for verbal theories that state signs
recommendation: State in the report that the rubric reads only the type label and cannot tell apart theories whose predictions are all directional.

title: How far human researchers agree when encoding is unmeasured; the pilot cannot stand in for it
component: Validation evidence for the package as a whole
recommendation: Run a preregistered study with human researchers before claiming reliability: at least two domain experts and two methodologists per theory, working from the primary papers, with an encoding protocol, independent construct matching by a second analyst, and the agreement measures used here (element kappa, edge Jaccard, independence-model kappa, derived-sign agreement, item and aggregate spread). Report the results in the documentation.
